speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the pelvic pain relieved by voiding, urgency, and recent dyspareunia, do you experience any vaginal itching, discharge, or a feeling of fullness in your pelvis? Have you noticed any changes in your bowel movements or stool consistency?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis / Painful Bladder Syndrome.

The pattern of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, urinary frequency, and dyspareunia without infection is classic for this condition. We will proceed with management focused on bladder pain syndrome rather than further infectious workup.
